questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving arrays — numeric sort.

options.misconception: Assuming sort leaves the original order
Picking the middle value
Treating the comparator as a swap count

questions.explanation: The comparator subtracts to sort numerically ascending, placing the smallest value 2 first. Without a comparator, sort would compare the numbers as strings. Run line by line, the closing console.log emits 2.
questions.hint: A comparator returning a minus b sorts numbers ascending.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving arrays — index of.

options.misconception: Using one-based indexing
Reporting the array length
Assuming the value is not found

questions.explanation: indexOf returns the zero-based position of the first match; 2897 sits at index zero here. A missing value would yield negative one instead. Walking the snippet in order, the output is 0.
questions.hint: JavaScript array positions begin at zero.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving arrays — find.
questions.explanation: find returns the first element satisfying the predicate; since 2898 exceeds one hundred, it is returned. If nothing matched, find would return undefined. Carrying the operation through gives 2898; common slips include returning the first element regardless of the test and using an index-style not-found marker.
questions.hint: find returns the element itself, not its position.
